question.problem:
The function $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x+3}{{x}^{2}+3x}$ has a discontinuity caused by a vertical asymptote at

$x=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes, let's start by factoring the expressions in the numerator and denominator. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x+3}{{x}^{2}+3x} \\  & =\frac{(x+3)(2x+1)}{x(x+3)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(x+3)}(2x+1)}{x\cancel{(x+3)}} \\  & =\frac{2x+1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the vertical asymptotes, we set the denominator equal to zero. Therefore, the function has a discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote at $x=0.$
